newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indofood 96 net seen within expectations.
newsitem.headline: Indofood 96 net seen within expectations.

text.p: Indonesia's largest noodle maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur increased its net profit to 351.31 billion rupiah in 1996 from 305.37 billion rupiah in 1995, but analysts said the results were within expectations.

"We expected Indofood's net profit to reach 351.8 billion rupiah last year. The firm booked a net profit of 351.31 billion rupiah, so it's still within our expectations," said one analyst from a large brokerage firm, who declined to be named.
The analyst said he expected the firm's net profit growth in 1997 to be relatively stable despite the firm's proposed acquisition of several sister companies within the Salim Group.
The analyst said noodle demand was expected to remain stable this year, while entries of some smaller noodle makers was unlikely to have much impact on Indofood's earnings.

"The results are still within our expectations of 350 billion rupiah. Nothing's surprising. This year we expect the firm's growth to remain stable," a senior research manager with a large foreign asset management firm said.
The research manager, who declined to be named, said players were still waiting for more details regarding Indofood's proposed acquisition plans.
"It's a good thing that they had reduced the cost of the acquisitions, but we need more details so that we could make a more accurate forecast for this year's results," he said.
Indofood said last week it had lowered the price of its proposed series of acquisitions to 1.55 trillion rupiah from the previous 1.75 trillion rupiah "to give more value to public shareholders."
The companies to be acquired include firms in the oil palm plantation business, a cooking oil producer and a palm oil trader.
